newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia Airlines says president 'relieved of duty'.
newsitem.headline: Croatia Airlines says president 'relieved of duty'.

text.p: Croatia Airlines' supervisory board has appointed Ivan Misetic, chief of protocol to President Franjo Tudjman, as company president to replace Matija Katicic, a company press officer said on Friday.
"Katicic was relieved of duty at his own request," she said. "The handover is in progress now."
The officer said Katicic gave no reason for resigning from the company he had headed since its foundation in 1990.
As a former sales director at Croatia Airlines and later director in charge of sales and marketing, Misetic is said by industry experts to be an able replacement.
He has headed Tudjman's protocol for the past two years, but has reportedly had his sights on the number one position at at the airline for some time.

The pressure on Katicic, who steered Croatia back to profitability last year, was said to have increased since his brother Martin Katicic was replaced from the helm of Privredna Banka that is now being overhauled.
The press officer would not comment on these rumours, and only said the decision to appoint a new company president was reached at a supervisory board meeting on Thursday afternoon.
"It happened very fast...but should not have any adverse effects," she added.
Croatia Airlines is negotiating financial support from banks for its order for six new Airbus A319s over the next three year.
But it may also buy other long-range planes by year 2006 as part of its plans to expand the current nine-plane fleet.

The company sees 1996 net profit at around $5 million thanks to a strong traffic increase and cost-cutting measures, compared to a $3.4 million net loss a year earlier. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
